title: Reserve GPU capacity across regions for latency/$ benchmark sweeps + launch-week guardrails
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
content:
## Background
We need predictable, repeatable benchmark sweeps across NA/EU/APAC regions for the public benchmark report. Previous sweeps had region-to-region variance driven by noisy neighbor / queueing effects and occasional capacity shortfalls (especially EU). To keep the methodology defensible, we need (1) reserved capacity for benchmark windows, (2) a schedule aligned to runner automation, (3) a documented fallback plan when a region is constrained, and (4) launch-week protection so the interactive page + results service stay stable under traffic.

This ticket covers the infra/fleet work: reserving GPU pools, scheduling windows, and defining fallback + on-call coverage.

Owners/partners:
- Owner: Harish Reddy (Capacity Ops)
- Fleet coordination: Vanessa Ortiz
- Reliability: Sean Gallagher / Neha Kapoor
- Benchmark leads: Jonas Weber / Claire Dubois / Rina Kobayashi

## Requirements / Acceptance criteria
1) Capacity reservations created and confirmed for benchmark sweep windows in all publishable regions.
2) Reservations specify: region, instance/GPU type, count, start/end time, and which fleet/pool is isolated.
3) A fallback plan is documented (what we do if a region cannot meet reservation, and how that impacts publication).
4) Communication plan: how we announce reservation windows + escalation path during runs.
5) Launch-week guardrails: ensure benchmark jobs do not collide with launch traffic; ensure results service has cache warm strategy and rate-limit settings are known to on-call.

## Proposed publishable regions (v1)
(Aligned with Product/PMM “supported vs experimental” guidance.)
- NA: us-east, us-west
- EU: eu-west, eu-central
- APAC: ap-southeast, ap-northeast

## Hardware / fleet assumptions
- Primary benchmark fleet: H100-80GB where available (preferred for consistency); A100-80GB in regions where H100 supply is insufficient.
- Jobs are run in isolated benchmark pools with fixed autoscaler settings (no opportunistic bursting during measurement).

## Reservation plan (target)
### Benchmark sweep windows (Weeks 3–5)
- Frequency: 3 full sweeps per region/model matrix (to satisfy stability gates), plus targeted reruns for outliers.
- Window size: 6 hours per region per sweep window.
- Concurrency: sized to match runner settings + stability gates (ENG-18521).

### Proposed allocations (initial)
NOTE: counts below are sized for parallel model runs + headroom for reruns within the same window.
- us-east: 16x H100
- us-west: 16x H100
- eu-west: 12x H100 (fallback to A100 if H100 short)
- eu-central: 8x H100 (or 8x A100 if needed)
- ap-southeast: 8x H100 (or 8x A100)
- ap-northeast: 8x H100 (or 8x A100)

We will not mix GPU types within a single region’s published numbers for a given sweep. If we must change GPU type, we treat that as a new sweep and re-run all models for that region before using numbers publicly.

## Fallback plan (when region is constrained)
### Trigger conditions
- Fleet cannot confirm reservation at least 48 hours before scheduled run.
- Reservation confirmed but on the day-of we see >10% job failures due to capacity/evictions OR sustained queueing leading to p95 variance beyond stability thresholds (ENG-18521).

### Fallback options (in priority order)
1) Shift the region’s window to off-peak (local time 00:00–06:00) within 24–48h.
2) Move the region to the secondary GPU type (H100 -> A100) ONLY if we can reserve enough to rerun the entire region/model matrix consistently.
3) Reduce the region’s published scope (publish fewer models in that region) ONLY with approval from Jonas/Claire + Henry Cho + Legal (Michael Grant/Sofia Mendes) because it impacts comparability and can be interpreted as cherry-picking.
4) Mark region as “experimental” and exclude from main report tables; keep internal for learning.

### Comms + decision authority
- Capacity/Fleet: Vanessa/Harish own feasibility + timing.
- Benchmark leads (Jonas/Claire/Rina) own whether partial data is publishable.
- PM/PMM (Henry/Soojin) own whether messaging changes.
- Legal owns final call on any “region coverage” statements.

## Scheduling + coordination
- Reservations will be created as named blocks in FleetDesk under project tag: BENCHMARK_REPORT_2025Q3.
- Runner schedule owner (Rina) gets a 1-week calendar view of reserved windows.
- #eng-infra + #eng-ml will receive a weekly post with upcoming windows + region status.
- Escalation: on-day issues go to #eng-oncall, primary: Sean Gallagher (SRE), secondary: Neha Kapoor.

## Launch-week guardrails
- Benchmark runs are paused during launch day (T-12h to T+24h) to avoid contention and confusing any “live” perceptions of the benchmark page.
- Fleet: keep a small warm pool in us-east/us-west for the results service and any demo traffic.
- Ensure CDN/cache warms (ENG-18566/ENG-18610) are executed before public announcement.

## Deliverables
- [x] FleetDesk reservations created and shared
- [x] Region-by-region confirmation and GPU types locked
- [x] Fallback playbook written and shared to on-call
- [x] Run windows added to shared calendar and communicated

## Open questions
- Do we need a separate reservation for “web ingestion/export” jobs (CSV/JSON publishing) or can it run in standard CI? (Leaning standard CI; minimal GPU needed.)
- Confirm final list of regions that Legal is comfortable with for any comparative phrasing.
